name: Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc. (operating and branded since January 2026 as Marsh)
headquarters: 1166 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10036-2774, United States; incorporated in Delaware
employees: Over 95,000 colleagues as of 31 December 2025 across 130 countries (FY2025 10-K). By segment: Risk and Insurance Services about 55,700 (Marsh Risk about 52,000, Marsh Re about 3,700); Consulting about 29,100 (Marsh People and Investments about 21,900, Marsh Management Consulting about 7,200)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Marsh McLennan is the world's largest insurance broker by revenue for the sixteenth consecutive year, and in January 2026 it retired the brand architecture that made it legible — the group now trades as Marsh, the broking arm is Marsh Risk, Mercer is Marsh People and Investments, and on 1 September 2026 the century-old Guy Carpenter name became Marsh Re. Its incumbency in the market this corpus covers is real but unevenly evidenced: independent sources name it repeatedly and specifically in AI data-centre risk — the Nimbus construction facility at USD 2.7bn, the Nimbus Casualty tower, the Stratus property exchange targeting USD 10bn on a single placement, and advisory roles on both sides of the USD 14bn Meta/BlackRock El Paso campus — while its battery-storage credentials appear only on its own website. BACKGROUND. Delaware-incorporated, headquartered at 1166 Avenue of the Americas, New York; over 95,000 colleagues in 130 countries; FY2025 revenue USD 26,981m (up 10 percent reported, 4 percent underlying) with adjusted EPS of USD 9.75. Two reportable segments: Risk and Insurance Services (USD 17,265m — Marsh Risk USD 14,366m, Marsh Re USD 2,496m) and Consulting (USD 9,794m — Marsh People and Investments USD 6,190m, Marsh Management Consulting USD 3,604m). The NYSE ticker changed from MMC to MRSH on 14 January 2026; the legal name and CUSIP did not change. McGriff Insurance Services was acquired for USD 7.75bn in cash, completed 18 November 2024 and funded with USD 7.25bn of senior notes. The Thrive programme, launched 16 October 2025, targets USD 400m of annual run-rate savings against about USD 500m of charges. Collection gap: no company-published history page exists at the company's own URL and no founding date is asserted here; the Global Insurance Market Index publishes no energy or renewables rate line; and the company names no competitor in any of its own materials reviewed for this dossier.
ecosystemRole: The larger of the two brokers this corpus places in insurance and risk transfer, and the counterparty that assembles the risk-transfer programme a project financing depends on — the seat kWh Analytics' own dossier identifies as 'the seat Marsh and Aon hold'. It works for the buyer, not the carrier: it builds the submission, markets it, structures the layers and advocates the claim, and is paid by commission out of the premium. Its distinctive contribution to this ecosystem is not placement volume but the construction of capacity where none existed — Nimbus for data-centre construction, Stratus for operational data-centre property at up to USD 10bn on one placement drawing on traditional and alternative capital, a renewables facility for sub-50 MW solar and storage, and the world's first green and blue hydrogen facility. It also sits on the challenger's own distribution: Marsh and its subsidiary McGriff together hold two of the eight seats on kWh Analytics' Broker Council in both published years, a quarter of that council in 2026, and neither readout discloses the common ownership.

productsAndServices.name: Marsh Risk — insurance broking and risk advisory
productsAndServices.description: The retail insurance broking and risk-advisory business, and the single largest revenue line in the company: USD 14,366m in FY2025, 54 percent of group revenue, about 52,000 colleagues. The 10-K calls it the 'world's leading insurance broker and risk advisor', selling 'risk management, insurance broking, insurance program design, risk consulting, analytical modeling and alternative risk financing services'. It works for the buyer of insurance, not the seller, and is paid by commission out of the premium or by a client fee. Until January 2026 this business was itself called Marsh; the group took that name and the broking arm became Marsh Risk.
highlights: FY2025 revenue USD 14,366m, up 15 percent GAAP and 4 percent underlying; Q2 2026 USD 4,071m, up 6 percent GAAP and 4 percent underlying

Compensation includes contingent commissions, which the 10-K says are taken 'primarily driven by MMA and parts of Marsh Risk's international operations' — the residue of the 2004-05 contingent-commission settlements
John Donnelly, President of Global Placement, is the named voice of the quarterly Global Insurance Market Index
Nick Studer became President and CEO on 1 April 2026, moving across from Oliver Wyman; Martin South, who held the seat, became Chief Client Officer of the group
productsAndServices.positioning: Self-described in the FY2025 10-K as the 'world's leading insurance broker and risk advisor'. Marsh names no competitor anywhere in its 10-K or in roughly fifty company pages reviewed for this dossier — the competitive framing in its own materials is generic ('competitive pressures... disintermediation'). Every comparison to Aon, WTW, Gallagher, Alliant, Brown & Brown, AmWins or CAC Specialty in this dossier is therefore third-party sourced.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct retail broking to large corporate and institutional buyers, with Marsh McLennan Agency as the separate middle-market retail channel and Victor Insurance Managers as the delegated-underwriting arm. Specialist risks are placed into the London and Lloyd's markets through Marsh Specialty.
targetSegments: Large corporate and multinational risk buyers
productsAndServices.roadmap: The Thrive programme, announced 16 October 2025, targets USD 400m of annual run-rate savings over three years against about USD 500m of restructuring charges, with part of the saving reinvested in talent and AI. USD 103m of those charges were taken in the first half of 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Digital infrastructure facilities — Nimbus, Nimbus Casualty and Stratus
productsAndServices.category: Risk and Insurance Services — facilities and exchanges
productsAndServices.description: Three purpose-built structures covering the data-centre lifecycle, all launched inside fifteen months, and the clearest evidence in this dossier of an incumbent broker building capacity products rather than only placing risk. Nimbus covers construction, Nimbus Casualty the excess liability tower above it, and Stratus the operational phase. Marsh calls Nimbus 'the first insurance facility built specifically for large-scale data center construction'.
highlights: Nimbus launched 16 June 2025 at EUR 1bn construction all-risks plus EUR 350m delay-in-start-up for the UK and Europe, on a panel of Lloyd's and company-market insurers
Nimbus expanded 26 January 2026 to USD 2.7bn inclusive of delay-in-start-up and business interruption, and widened to the UK, US, Canada, Europe, Australia and New Zealand

Nimbus Casualty launched 19 February 2026: up to USD 75m of excess general liability for US digital-infrastructure construction attaching at a minimum of USD 25m, on an A+ rated Lloyd's and London panel, written on Marsh Risk's proprietary XSellence follow-form

Stratus launched 26 August 2026: up to USD 10bn of property capacity on a single placement for the global exposures of US-domiciled companies, drawing on 30 traditional and alternative capital providers, structured as an exchange on a prior-submit basis rather than fixed committed shares
Mike Mathews was appointed to the newly created role of Global Digital Infrastructure Leader on 18 December 2025, two months before Nimbus Casualty and eight before Stratus
productsAndServices.positioning: Stratus is the structure that distinguishes this line: an exchange admitting alternative capital alongside traditional insurers for operational data-centre property risk, at a limit no single tower has previously offered for the class. It is the operational-phase extension of Nimbus and it is how a broker earns from placement design in a market where the property rate index fell 12 percent year on year.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Placed through Marsh Risk's own broking teams into panel facilities and, for Stratus, into an exchange where underwriters assess each submission and may decline rather than committing a fixed share.
targetSegments: US-domiciled digital-infrastructure owners with global exposures
Construction contractors on large-scale data-centre projects
productsAndServices.roadmap: Marsh states that Stratus will expand into inland marine, cyber and casualty, aiming at 'a single point of access for clients across a project's full lifecycle from construction through operation'. No delivery date has been published.

productsAndServices.name: Marsh Re — reinsurance broking and capital (formerly Guy Carpenter)
productsAndServices.description: The reinsurance intermediary, and the business whose client is an insurance company rather than a policyholder: it designs and places the treaties that let a carrier write more risk than its own capital would allow, and advises on how much risk to keep. The 10-K describes 'specialized reinsurance broking, strategic advisory and actuarial services, and analytics solutions'. FY2025 revenue USD 2,496m from about 3,700 colleagues. The Guy Carpenter name, in use for over a century, was retired on 1 September 2026 — eight days before this dossier was written.
highlights: Second globally on FY2024 reinsurance broking revenue (USD 2.544bn) behind Aon Reinsurance Solutions (USD 2.656bn), but ahead of it in H1 2025 (USD 1.952bn against USD 1.877bn) per Reinsurance News

The top tier of Aon, Marsh Re, Gallagher Re and Howden Re holds more than 85 percent of reinsurance premium per The Insurer — though Reinsurance News cautions that its own revenue basis is not clean broking revenue and no source reconciles a market-share figure

Revenue fell 2 percent in Q2 2026 on both a reported and an underlying basis, to USD 664m, despite double-digit new business and high-90s retention — the decline is commission compression as property-catastrophe rates fell 16 percent at the midyear renewal

Reported double-digit risk-adjusted rate reductions on loss-free programmes at the January 2026 renewal, with dedicated reinsurance capital up 9 percent and catastrophe-bond notional outstanding above USD 58bn
Dean Klisura, its President and CEO, called data centres 'the single biggest new business opportunity in 2026 for both cedents and reinsurers', with up to USD 10bn of new premium entering the market
Platforms: GC AdvantagePoint catastrophe analytics, Edge, Marketplace, Structured Solutions, and Marsh Securities for insurance-linked securities and catastrophe bonds
productsAndServices.positioning: The reinsurance seat is where this company touches the capital that ultimately absorbs a battery or data-centre loss, and it is also the line the softening market is hurting most. Its Marine and Energy page names London Market Excess Loss and global retrocession but names no renewable energy, offshore wind, battery storage or power product, and GC AdvantagePoint publishes no renewables module — so a renewables reinsurance capability, if one exists, is not on its website.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct broking to insurance and reinsurance companies, mutuals, agencies and captives, with capital-markets execution through Marsh Securities.
productsAndServices.roadmap: The rename to Marsh Re was originally reported as taking effect from 2027 and was pulled forward to 1 September 2026; no source explains the acceleration.

productsAndServices.name: Energy and Power — renewable energy, and the facilities that sit under it
productsAndServices.category: Risk and Insurance Services — industry practice
productsAndServices.description: The industry practice through which this company meets battery storage and renewables. It publishes sub-sector pages for battery energy storage, solar, onshore and offshore wind, hydrogen, hydropower, geothermal, biomass, carbon capture, oil and gas, and power and utility, plus risk engineering and due-diligence advisory. The scale figures are the company's own and are not independently corroborated: more than 700 Energy and Power specialists, more than 400 renewable-energy specialists, more than 650 GW of renewable projects supported and more than 162 GW of solar.
highlights: Marsh Specialty Renewables Facility, launched 2 May 2022: mid-scale solar and battery storage under 50 MW per project in the United States, covering construction all risk, operational all risk and general and excess liability with optional replacement cost and business interruption, liability up to USD 25m, quotes in three to five business days

Hydrogen facility, launched 22 August 2022 and described by the company as the world's first for green and blue hydrogen: up to USD 300m per risk globally, led by Liberty Specialty Markets and AIG, covering construction, start-up and the first year of operation including contingent delay-in-start-up

Tax Investment Default Insurance (2024) protects renewable developers against tax-credit investor default under Inflation Reduction Act transferability, with lenders nameable as loss payee; the separate ITC and PTC tax-insurance line covers begun-construction, continuity, qualified-basis, structural and repowering disallowance, and storage where 'battery storage integrated into solar facilities' is covered while 'standalone storage discussions remain ongoing'

Amy Barnes has been Global Head of Energy and Power since 19 March 2025, holding that role jointly with Head of Climate and Sustainability Strategy — the energy practice and the climate mandate sit with one person

COLLECTION GAP: no independent source located in this research names this company as a protagonist in any battery-storage placement. Its BESS credentials — a USD 200m Asia facility, 3.8 GW of UK grid-scale storage placed, a 60-strong London power and renewables team — appear only on its own website
productsAndServices.positioning: Its published battery-storage guidance describes insurer requirements in engineering terms — separation between enclosures, routing power to the grid separately from the battery, fire-protection features — while naming no code, standard or certification body. Seven company documents across four web properties spanning 2021 to 2026 were examined for this dossier and not one names UL, UL 9540A, NFPA 855, DNV, CSA, TUV, IEC, IEEE or FM Global. The closest the battery page comes is 'varying installation, operation, and engineering standards around the world' — invoking standards as a problem while naming none. That unnamed certification layer is precisely the space DNV and kWh Analytics occupy.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Retail broking through Marsh Risk's energy and power teams, into panel facilities for mid-scale and specialist risks and into the open London market for large accounts.
targetSegments: Lenders and tax-equity investors requiring insurance conditions
productsAndServices.roadmap: Standalone-storage tax insurance is stated as under discussion and not yet offered. Collection note: this dossier could not locate the company's onshore wind, offshore wind or carbon-capture expertise pages at any URL, and the Wayback Machine holds no snapshot of the paths tried — so the company's wind and carbon-capture positioning is uncovered here rather than absent.

productsAndServices.name: Marsh McLennan Agency — the middle market
productsAndServices.description: The middle-market retail platform, a wholly owned subsidiary selling business insurance, employee health and benefits, retirement and private-client solutions to small and midsize organisations in the United States and Canada. The company describes it as the fifth-largest insurance broker in the United States with annualised revenues of approximately USD 5bn. It is the vehicle through which McGriff was absorbed, and the part of the business where contingent commissions are concentrated.
highlights: McGriff Insurance Services acquired for USD 7.75bn in cash, completed 18 November 2024, bringing about USD 1.3bn of annual revenue and more than 3,500 colleagues; funded with cash plus USD 7.25bn of senior notes issued in November 2024, with an assumed deferred tax asset of about USD 500m

The chief executive declared the McGriff integration complete in the FY2025 results, though USD 215m of integration and retention costs were charged in FY2025 and a further USD 89m in the first half of 2026
No McGriff-named entity appears in the FY2025 subsidiary list, consistent with full absorption
Bolt-ons continued through 2026: TriBridge Partners completed 1 June 2026, and Accel Holdings agreed 10 August 2026 with terms undisclosed

The 10-K states that contingent commissions are taken 'primarily driven by MMA and parts of Marsh Risk's international operations' — the residue of the 2004-05 settlements, and a live conflict surface for a broker advising project developers
productsAndServices.positioning: Independent commentators called the McGriff consideration 'rich at almost 6 times revenue' and questioned whether it will prove value-creative. Aon's agreement on 30 August 2026 to buy USI for USD 17.0bn is a direct answer in the same market, and it is the competitive fact this dossier is closest in time to.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Retail agency distribution across US and Canadian regional offices, acquired and organic.
targetSegments: Small and midsize US and Canadian businesses
productsAndServices.roadmap: The Accel Holdings acquisition was expected to close in the third quarter of 2026; no completion has been published.

productsAndServices.name: Risk analytics and data platforms
productsAndServices.description: The proprietary analytics layer the company sells as its differentiation from a pure placement broker, and the layer its own strategy statements now put at the centre. It spans the Blue[i] suite on the broking side, Sentrisk on supply chain, catastrophe analytics on the reinsurance side, and a loss-data library assembled from the company's own claims record.
highlights: Blue[i] modules published: Risk Program Analytics, Risk Finance Optimization, Risk Appetite, Property, D&O, Cyber, Claims, Casualty, Cost of Risk Analytics and PEMA Insights

Sentrisk, launched 2 May 2024, maps supply chains with AI and geospatial satellite imaging and models natural hazard, geopolitical, climate, reputational, single-supplier and geographic-concentration risk; built jointly by the broking and consulting arms
Marsh BLAST Powered by MaxLoss for catastrophe and loss modelling on the power and utility side; Natural Catastrophe Analytics; a Global Loss Data Library; and an Economic Cost of Risk measure
GC AdvantagePoint on the reinsurance side, with Event Impact and Underwriter+ modules

Over 46,000 colleagues had completed AI Academy credentials by the FY2025 10-K, against a workforce of over 95,000 — roughly half the firm credentialed on AI since the programme launched in August 2024
productsAndServices.positioning: Analytics is the answer this company gives to two different pressures at once: a softening rate cycle that shrinks commission, and the February 2026 fear that AI could disintermediate broking altogether. Whether it answers either is not yet visible in the organic growth rate.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with broking and consulting engagements rather than licensed standalone; no published pricing.
targetSegments: Risk managers building a cost-of-risk case
productsAndServices.roadmap: The Business and Client Services unit created in the October 2025 reorganisation centralises technology, data and operations under the Chief Information and Operations Officer, and is the stated delivery vehicle for expanded AI deployment funded out of the Thrive savings.

productsAndServices.name: Captives, delegated underwriting and alternative risk
productsAndServices.category: Risk and Insurance Services — alternative risk
productsAndServices.description: The routes around a conventional policy: a captive the client owns, a protected cell it rents, or an underwriting agency that binds a carrier's paper. This is the part of the business that converts premium into retained capital, and it is the structural answer for risks the open market will not price — which is the position new energy technology usually starts from.
highlights: Marsh Captive Solutions reports USD 79.1bn of gross written premium across the captives it manages in its 2026 benchmarking report

Marsh Nexus Captive Solution launched 16 June 2026, a protected cell structure through the company's Mangrove Protected Cell Company domiciled in Washington DC, for multinationals with more than USD 3m of annual non-US employee-benefits spend

Victor Insurance Managers is the delegated-underwriting arm — a managing general agent inside a broker, which is the same seat kWh Analytics occupies from outside. The 10-K does not break out Victor's premium volume; third-party reporting of USD 3-4bn is not company-sourced

Parametric solutions are published for cyclone, earthquake, drought, wind speed and rainfall triggers and for supply-chain disruption — but the current parametrics page names no renewables, solar, wind-generation or hail application
productsAndServices.positioning: Owning both a broker and a managing general agent is the structural tension in this line: Victor binds carrier paper in the same market where Marsh Risk represents the buyer. The company does not address the conflict in its published materials.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Captive management fees, cell rental, and delegated underwriting commission through Victor.
targetSegments: Large corporates with sufficient loss experience to retain risk
Programme sponsors in classes the open market underserves

productsAndServices.name: Marsh People and Investments, and Marsh Management Consulting
productsAndServices.description: The Consulting segment — the former Mercer and Oliver Wyman — at USD 9,794m of FY2025 revenue and about 29,100 colleagues. Mercer, renamed Marsh People and Investments, advises on the health, wealth and career needs of a workforce and runs an investment business; Marsh Management Consulting, which includes Oliver Wyman, Lippincott and NERA, sells management consulting, brand strategy and economic analysis. It is not a risk-transfer business, and it is the half of the company that is currently growing fastest.
highlights: FY2025: Mercer USD 6,190m (up 8 percent GAAP, 4 percent underlying); Marsh Management Consulting USD 3,604m (up 6 percent GAAP and underlying)

Q2 2026: Consulting underlying growth of 8 percent against Risk and Insurance Services at 3 percent, with Marsh Management Consulting alone at 13 percent underlying — growth has moved from broking to consulting
Oliver Wyman contributed the supply-chain modelling behind Sentrisk and was one of four businesses credited on the July 2026 digital-infrastructure research
Nick Studer moved from chief executive of Oliver Wyman to run Marsh Risk on 1 April 2026, and Ted Moynihan took the consulting seat
productsAndServices.positioning: For this corpus the consulting arm matters mainly as the source of the company's published research on data-centre power economics and as the reason a broker can be engaged as technical advisor on a financing rather than only as a placement agent — the role it took for the BlackRock funds on the El Paso campus.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct consulting engagements and retained advisory.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Under the rebrand the individual business names migrate through 2027; Oliver Wyman goes to market as 'Oliver Wyman, a Marsh business' rather than being renamed outright.

productsAndServices.name: Market intelligence — the published research that sets the vocabulary
productsAndServices.description: A quarterly rate index, an annual global risk survey run with the World Economic Forum, and a body of sector research. For a broker this is marketing in the form of measurement, and it matters here because the rate index is one of the few public series against which the cost of insuring an energy asset can be tracked.
highlights: Global Insurance Market Index, Q2 2026 published 23 July 2026: composite rates down 6 percent, an eighth consecutive quarterly decline; property down 12 percent globally and 13 percent in the United States; casualty up 2 percent globally and 7 percent in the United States; financial and professional down 3 percent; cyber down 4 percent
John Donnelly, President of Global Placement: 'Current market conditions are likely to persist absent a severe northern hemisphere storm season or string of major natural catastrophes'

COLLECTION GAP: the index breaks out property, casualty, financial and professional, and cyber. It publishes no energy, renewables or battery-storage line, so no company-sourced rate series exists for the assets this corpus covers

Global Risks Report 2026 with the World Economic Forum, published 14 January 2026 from 1,300 experts and 11,000 business leaders: extreme weather third among immediate risks, environmental risks dominating the ten-year horizon, and 57 percent of respondents predicting a turbulent decade
100 Largest Losses in the Hydrocarbon Industry, 29th edition, published 15 June 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: The rate index is quoted across the trade press as a market benchmark, which gives the company agenda-setting weight no competitor's research matches at the same cadence. Its silence on renewables rates is therefore conspicuous rather than neutral.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Published free; a client-acquisition and agenda-setting instrument, not a product.
targetSegments: Risk managers and chief financial officers

recentDevelopments.headline: Guy Carpenter formally becomes Marsh Re, retiring a reinsurance broking name in use for over a century; marked by two publications ahead of the Rendez-Vous de Septembre
recentDevelopments.read: Eight days before this dossier was written. The rename was originally reported as taking effect from 2027 and was pulled forward; no source explains the acceleration. Nine of the top ten reinsurance brokers now trade under their group's primary broking name.

recentDevelopments.headline: Stratus launched — up to USD 10bn of property capacity on a single placement for operational digital infrastructure, drawing on 30 traditional and alternative capital providers on a prior-submit exchange basis
recentDevelopments.read: The most consequential product in this dossier and the answer to Aon overtaking Nimbus on construction capacity: rather than raise a construction facility, Marsh built an exchange on the operational side and admitted alternative capital to it. No first-party release was located.

recentDevelopments.headline: Marsh Risk named Business Insurance's 2026 US Insurance Awards Broker Team of the Year, over Aon, EPIC, Spring Consulting and WTW, for the TerraPower Natrium placement at Kemmerer, Wyoming
recentDevelopments.read: A third-party jury judging capability rather than a revenue table. The placement was over USD 2bn and 128 percent oversubscribed with Munich Re leading, after two years spent educating more than 80 insurers on an advanced reactor — capability built for exactly the nuclear-for-data-centres demand this corpus tracks.

recentDevelopments.headline: Katie Burke, US specialty energy and power growth leader at Marsh Risk, describes 'unprecedented' new-business growth as hyperscalers become power-generation companies; the same report describes battery storage as an increasingly popular means to stabilise data-centre loads
recentDevelopments.read: The only independent source that bridges this corpus's two halves through Marsh: its storage relevance runs through data-centre power procurement, not through utility-scale renewables. Marsh's power practice is reported working closely with its construction team on the data-centre build.

recentDevelopments.headline: Marsh McLennan Agency agrees to acquire Accel Holdings, Inc. of Waverly, Iowa — commercial and personal lines, employee benefits, agribusiness, wealth management and retirement advisory; terms undisclosed, expected to close in Q3 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The middle-market bolt-on programme continues three weeks before Aon commits USD 17bn to the same market.

recentDevelopments.headline: Marsh reported as advising both sides of the approximately USD 14bn Meta and BlackRock El Paso data-centre campus — project risk analysis and insurance services for Meta, and technical advisor to the BlackRock funds
recentDevelopments.read: Simultaneously the strongest evidence of incumbency in AI-infrastructure risk and an independently flagged governance question. The deal is 80 percent BlackRock funds and 20 percent Meta, about 1 GW of compute, with a USD 12.5bn debt package and a Meta residual-value guarantee of about USD 13bn.

recentDevelopments.headline: Global Insurance Market Index for Q2 2026: composite commercial rates down 6 percent, an eighth consecutive quarterly decline, with property down 12 percent globally and 13 percent in the United States
recentDevelopments.read: The softening is the central pressure on this business model: commission is a percentage of a shrinking premium, and the property line falling 12 percent is a roughly six-percentage-point drag on underlying growth.

relationships.note: Marsh holds a named seat on kWh Analytics' Renewable Energy Broker Council in both published years, and through McGriff it holds a second — two of the eight seats.
relationships.context:
Luke Slemeck represents Marsh on the council in both the 2025 readout (published by Insurance Journal on 2 July 2025) and the 2026 readout (published by pv magazine USA on 9 June 2026). Todd Burack represents McGriff in both. McGriff has been a Marsh McLennan subsidiary since the acquisition completed on 18 November 2024, so both readouts post-date the close — and neither discloses the common ownership. In 2026 that is a quarter of the challenger's own distribution advisory board held by one group.

The relationship is distribution, not competition: kWh Analytics is a managing general agent that binds carrier paper and reaches the market through specialist brokers, and Marsh is one of those brokers. Slemeck's contributions are on solar hail resilience and long-run insurability rather than on battery storage — in 2026: 'Resilience isn't really about cost savings. It's about continued insurability. If you do nothing and the market hardens, you're going to have a very hard time getting insurance.'

relationships.note: The other incumbent in this segment: first and second in every independent global broker ranking located, and currently in litigation with each other.
relationships.context:
AM Best's ranking on 2025 total revenue puts Marsh first for a sixteenth consecutive year at USD 26.98bn against Aon at USD 17.20bn, and Business Insurance's 2026 Broker Profiles ranks them first and second. The measure matters: AM Best's total bundles this company's consulting businesses, which are not broking, and no source published since 2018 offers a clean broking-only comparison of the two.

On data-centre construction capacity Aon is ahead. Its Data Center Lifecycle Insurance Program went from USD 1.5bn at launch in July 2025 to USD 2.5bn in January 2026, USD 3.5bn in April and USD 5bn in July 2026, against Nimbus at USD 2.7bn — which is the context for Stratus being built on the operational side rather than the construction side.

They are also adverse in court. Marsh USA sued Aon and Robert McDonough in federal court in New York in April 2025 after McDonough and nineteen others — about 70 percent of his direct reports — resigned within a 38-minute window on 10 March 2025, with McDonough becoming chief executive of Aon's North American construction, infrastructure and surety group seven days later. Aon declined to comment.

relationships.via: project risk analysis and insurance services
relationships.note: Reported as providing project risk analysis and insurance services to Meta on the El Paso data-centre campus — and simultaneously as technical advisor to the BlackRock funds on the other side of the same transaction.
relationships.context:
The campus is a roughly USD 14bn development, about 1 GW of compute, structured as 80 percent BlackRock funds and 20 percent Meta, with roughly USD 4.9bn of BlackRock cash, a USD 12.5bn debt package, about USD 2.3bn of Meta land and construction-in-progress contribution, and a Meta residual-value guarantee of about USD 13bn. Meta is the sole initial occupant.

Insurance Business headlined the arrangement 'Marsh on both sides of the table' — the company is reported acting for the tenant and advising the investor. The article frames specialist advisors as 'a precondition for getting the financing across the line', which is the clearest single statement in this corpus of why a broker sits inside an AI-infrastructure capital structure rather than beside it. This dossier records the arrangement as reported and does not adjudicate the governance question it raises.

relationships.note: Adjacent seats at the same financial close rather than a commercial relationship: DNV certifies and writes recommended practice, this company advises the buyer and places the risk. Recorded because each documents an absence on the other's side.
relationships.context:
The overlap is advisory rather than commercial. DNV certifies and writes recommended practices, including RP-0043 for grid-scale storage; Marsh advises the buyer and places the risk. The DNV dossier records that no insurer document it found cites RP-0043 and that 'Munich Re and Marsh name no certifier', citing Marsh's own battery-energy-storage page.

This dossier's research confirms and widens that finding: across seven Marsh battery-storage documents spanning 2021 to 2026 and four company web properties, no certification body or standard is named — not UL, UL 9540A, NFPA 855, DNV, CSA, TUV, IEC, IEEE or FM Global. Marsh states insurer requirements in engineering terms — separation between enclosures, routing power to the grid independently of the battery, fire-protection features — while the codes that specify them go unnamed. Aon's published battery guidance does the same, naming only SCOR's 2022 handbook. The unnamed certification layer is the space DNV occupies, and neither broker points to it.

policyExposure.regime: US state insurance licensing and surplus lines
policyExposure.exposure: The FY2025 10-K states that 'All U.S. states and most foreign jurisdictions require insurance market intermediaries and related service providers (such as insurance brokers, agents and consultants, reinsurance brokers and managing general agents) to hold an individual or company license.' The licensing perimeter covers the broking arm, the reinsurance arm, the middle-market agency and Victor Insurance Managers as a delegated underwriter. It is also the regime under which the company's facilities reach non-admitted capacity: the Nimbus and Nimbus Casualty towers sit on Lloyd's and London-market paper, which is surplus-lines from a US buyer's perspective and therefore outside state guaranty-fund protection.

The 10-K discloses that the broking arm 'receives other compensation from insurance companies, which includes... contingent commissions, based on factors such as volume or profitability of Marsh Risk's placements, primarily driven by MMA and parts of Marsh Risk's international operations.' That carve-out is the residue of the 2004-05 New York Attorney General matter, in which the company was found to have designated which insurer's bid would win and to have instructed insurers to submit inflated, intentionally uncompetitive bids, funded by undisclosed contingent commissions; it settled with an USD 850m policyholder fund covering inceptions from 1 January 2001 to 31 December 2004 and eliminated contingent compensation from 1 January 2005, with further state settlements in 2008. The practice has since returned in the middle market — which is where McGriff sits.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company's own stated position is disclosure rather than abstention: contingent commissions are described in the 10-K and confined to the middle-market agency and parts of international operations rather than the large-account US broking business.

policyExposure.exposure: 'Our business is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority in the U.K. The FCA licenses insurance and reinsurance intermediaries and evaluates related criteria such as professional competence, financial capacity and professional indemnity insurance requirements.' The UK perimeter matters disproportionately here because the London market is where the digital-infrastructure facilities are placed and where Marsh Re trades.

policyExposure.regime: Errors and omissions and fiduciary duty
policyExposure.exposure: The 10-K's risk-factor summary states: 'We are subject to significant uninsured exposures arising from errors and omissions, breach of fiduciary duty and other claims.' This is the risk factor with a live number attached. In Q1 2026 the company recorded a gross liability of USD 425m over Australian proceedings related to Greensill, after court-sponsored mediation in March 2026, and called the figure provisional with additional charges possible. Claimants across eleven consolidated Federal Court proceedings — the Greensill administrators, Credit Suisse and two of its funds, White Oak, Greensill Bank AG, Insurance Australia Limited and the BCC/Tokio Marine parties — seek figures reported both as about USD 5bn plus interest and as about A$7bn; no source reconciles the two.
policyExposure.mitigation: Marsh Ltd settled with White Oak in May 2025 for an undisclosed sum the company states was recovered through its own errors-and-omissions insurance, and Marsh Ltd, Marsh Pty Ltd and other parties settled with Greensill Bank and its insolvency administrator in June 2026. A separate and far smaller matter — Match Group's April 2026 New York suit alleging a claim was notified to the insurer roughly 57 hours after the policy expired — seeks about USD 3.9m.

policyExposure.exposure: The 10-K names the EU General Data Protection Regulation, the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act, Australia's CPS 234, and 'emerging AI-related laws such as the EU's AI Act'. The exposure is unusually concrete for this company because its stated differentiation is analytics: the Blue[i] suite, the Sentrisk supply-chain platform built with the consulting arm, and an AI Academy through which more than 46,000 of about 95,000 colleagues had been credentialed by the FY2025 10-K. A risk factor states the business 'could be negatively affected if we are not able to develop and implement improvements in technology or respond effectively to the threat of digital disruption and other technological change such as AI' — and on 9 February 2026 the market priced exactly that threat, marking the shares down 7.51 percent in a session.

The 10-K states the company is 'subject to various financial crime laws and regulations through our activities of associated persons, the products and services we provide and our business and client relationships... relate to, among other areas, sanctions and export control, anti-bribery, anti-corruption, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist financing', and its forward-looking statements name the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the UK Anti Bribery Act and 'domestic and international sanctions regimes'. For a broker the exposure runs through placement: the identity of every carrier on a tower and every party to a reinsurance treaty is a compliance question as much as a credit one.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that this company is the incumbent of the insurance-and-risk-transfer segment on every independent measure available, and that its position is not in doubt. Basis: AM Best ranks it first among global brokers on 2025 total revenue at USD 26.98bn for a sixteenth consecutive year, against Aon at USD 17.20bn — more than the third, fourth and fifth brokers combined; Business Insurance ranks it first in its 2026 Broker Profiles and first among the largest brokers of US business; and its reinsurance arm was second globally on FY2024 revenue inside a top tier holding more than 85 percent of reinsurance premium. No independent source located disputes the leadership position.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that its incumbency in the market this corpus actually covers is evidenced by data centres, not by batteries, and that the dossier's claim should be scoped accordingly. Basis: independent trade press names this company repeatedly and specifically in AI-infrastructure risk — Nimbus at USD 2.7bn, Nimbus Casualty at USD 75m excess of USD 25m, Stratus targeting USD 10bn on a single placement, a dedicated Global Digital Infrastructure Contract Advisory Group established in January 2026, advisory roles on both sides of the USD 14bn Meta and BlackRock El Paso campus, and a Business Insurance award for a USD 2bn advanced-reactor placement. Against that, outside the two kWh Analytics Broker Council readouts, no independent source located names this company in a battery-storage placement. Its BESS credentials — a USD 200m Asia facility, 3.8 GW of UK grid-scale storage placed, a 60-strong London team — appear only on its own website.

3. **(High confidence)** We assess that neither of this segment's two incumbents anchors its battery-storage guidance to a named standard, and that this is a structural feature of broker-authored risk guidance rather than an oversight by one firm. Basis: seven Marsh battery documents across four company web properties spanning 2021 to 2026 name no certification body or standard — not UL, UL 9540A, NFPA 855, DNV, CSA, TUV, IEC, IEEE or FM Global — and the closest the battery page comes is 'varying installation, operation, and engineering standards around the world', invoking standards as a problem while naming none. Aon's battery guidance does the same, citing only SCOR's 2022 handbook. Both describe insurer requirements in engineering terms — Marsh on separation between enclosures and independent grid routing, Aon on 'three metres or more of spacing'. NFPA 855 is the code that specifies separation. The brokers state the requirement and leave the code unnamed, which is precisely the space a certifier or a data-priced managing general agent occupies.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the facility-and-exchange model is this company's answer to a softening market, and that it is a durable one. Basis: its own index reports an eighth consecutive quarterly decline with property down 12 percent globally, which is a roughly six-percentage-point drag on underlying growth, and commission is a percentage of a shrinking premium. Its response has been to build capacity products that earn from placement design rather than from rate — the Renewables Facility, the hydrogen facility, Nimbus, Nimbus Casualty and Stratus, which admits alternative capital alongside traditional insurers on a prior-submit basis. Confidence is moderate rather than high because no source discloses what these facilities earn.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that Stratus was built on the operational side because the construction side had already been lost to Aon. Basis: Nimbus went to USD 2.7bn in January 2026 and has not moved since, while Aon's Data Center Lifecycle Insurance Program went to USD 3.5bn in April 2026 and USD 5bn in July 2026, and Aon also claims a first-ever data-centre reinsurance treaty aligning up to USD 5bn of capital behind a single insurer. Stratus followed on 26 August 2026, addressing the operational phase Nimbus does not cover, at a limit no competitor has matched. The sequence is consistent with a competitive response; no source states the motive, so this is inference and is labelled as such.

6. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that this company's reinsurance arm has no published renewables or storage franchise, and that its stated appetite is digital infrastructure instead. Basis: across Marsh Re's two flagship September 2026 publications — the 2027 Renewal Outlook and the Global Specialties 2026 Market Update — battery storage and solar are named zero times in the extractable text and renewable energy once, as a portfolio-boundary complication inside marine and energy; data centres appear eleven times and are called 'the standout growth story', with cedents 'seeing two or three opportunities each week'. Its Marine and Energy practice page names no renewables, wind, storage or power product. Confidence is moderate on the zeros rather than high because the counts come from locally extracted PDF text, which can under-capture image-rendered sections.

7. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the group's growth has moved from broking to consulting, and that this cuts against the segment's own framing of the company. Basis: underlying growth halved from 7 percent in FY2024 to 4 percent in FY2025, and in Q2 2026 Consulting grew 8 percent underlying against Risk and Insurance Services at 3 percent, with Marsh Management Consulting alone at 13 percent. The reinsurance arm shrank 2 percent. Independent commentary put the FY2025 figure below every major listed competitor except Brown & Brown — Aon delivered 6 percent — and Goldman Sachs held an outright Sell until 20 October 2025, upgrading on logic that included the 2026 organic estimate sitting below expected US nominal GDP growth.

8. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the group holds a structurally unusual position inside the challenger's own distribution, and that no party has disclosed it. Basis: Marsh and McGriff each hold a named seat on kWh Analytics' Renewable Energy Broker Council in both published years — two of eight seats, a quarter of the 2026 council — and McGriff has been a subsidiary since 18 November 2024, so both readouts post-date the close. Neither readout, and no source located, notes the common ownership. The relationship is distribution rather than rivalry: kWh binds carrier paper and reaches the market through specialist brokers, and this company is two of them.

9. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the February 2026 AI-disintermediation repricing was an overreaction to a personal-lines event, but that the underlying question is not settled. Basis: Insurify's ChatGPT-native comparison app took WTW down 12 percent in its worst session since 2008, Aon down 9.3 percent and this company down 7.51 percent, with Bank of America sizing about USD 15bn of low-complexity commissions at risk; Bloomberg Intelligence, Wolfe Research and Goldman Sachs all called it overdone on the grounds that the product was personal lines while the majors are commercial. The company's own answer is analytics and an AI Academy through which more than 46,000 of about 95,000 colleagues have been credentialed. Confidence is low because no evidence yet exists either way on whether commercial broking is exposed to the same mechanism.

10. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the January 2026 rebrand carries an unpriced execution risk that will not be visible in reported numbers for some time. Basis: the group retired four established professional-services brands at once, two of them more than a century old, and moved its ticker in the same month; Guy Carpenter became Marsh Re on 1 September 2026, eight days before this dossier, and the remaining migrations run through 2027. A broking business's asset is a relationship and a broker-of-record letter, both of which travel with people rather than brands — but the sector is simultaneously in a lateral-hire litigation wave in which this company is a plaintiff against Aon, Howden and Alliant. No source connects the rebrand to attrition, and this is flagged as a thing to watch rather than a finding.

Q3 2026 results, expected mid-October 2026 (unconfirmed): whether Marsh Re's revenue decline deepens past the 2 percent of Q2, and whether Risk and Insurance Services underlying growth stays below Consulting's. A third consecutive quarter of that pattern would confirm Judgment 7; a reinsurance recovery would refute it.

Stratus placement disclosure: any statement of capacity actually bound rather than targeted. More than USD 4bn of verbal commitments against a USD 10bn target was reported at launch; conversion is the test of Judgment 4.

Aon's completion of the USI acquisition, expected Q4 2026: a competitor at about USD 19.9bn of brokerage revenue against this company's USD 26.66bn narrows a gap that has been stable for sixteen years. Watch also whether the middle-market contest changes what contingent commissions this company discloses.

Any Marsh publication that names a battery-storage standard — UL 9540A, NFPA 855 or a certification body. That would refute Judgment 3 and would signal that broker guidance is converging on the certification layer.

The Greensill provision: the USD 425m is explicitly provisional against claims reported at about USD 5bn plus interest and about A$7bn. Any revision moves the GAAP line materially and tests the errors-and-omissions risk factor.

Whether a first-party press release for Stratus ever appears. A USD 10bn product published as a page under the technology vertical, absent from the newsroom and uncross-referenced by the vertical's own data-centre services page, is either a soft launch or an organisational seam.
